editorial.headline: Forest Plant Retail: Nationally Open, Blocked for PMA Registration in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity is open to full foreign ownership nationally, yet Bali’s permanent PMA moratorium prevents registration there today.
editorial.body:
Foreign investors cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali today. That is the decisive local fact, even though the national position is fully open to foreign ownership. The activity is the retail trade of forestry plants, forestry seeds and seedlings, and parts of forestry plants. Its scope also places it beyond direct sales: this is a defined retail activity for bringing forestry planting material and related plant parts to market.

The permitted business scales are broad: Micro, Small, Medium and Large enterprises may undertake the activity. That breadth matters because the code is not framed as a niche reserved for one size of operator. A business may be established across the full stated range of scales, provided its actual operations remain within retail trading of forestry plants, seeds, seedlings and plant parts. The record does not extend the activity into cultivation, production or any other commercial function; its centre of gravity is retail trade.

At the national level, the PMA status is open, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, the national framework allows full foreign ownership for this activity. The stated basis is Presidential Regulations 10/2021 and 49/2021. For a founder assessing Indonesia at national level, that is a clear opening: foreign capital is not capped below full ownership for this code.

Bali reaches a different operational outcome. For the Large-scale registration in this record, OSS assigns Low or Medium-Low risk across every scope. Bali’s island-wide, permanent moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities from PMA registration. The result is not a reduction in the national ownership ceiling; it is a local bar on PMA registration in Bali for this activity. The distinction is essential: nationally, full foreign ownership is open; in Bali, the applicable risk classification brings the activity within the moratorium. The local position is recorded as blocked by risk class, under the Governor’s letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP.
